🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 17 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Keralam’s State Planning Board moots a Partnership Cell for forging a ‘partnership economy’

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The proposed cell will focus on forging partnerships among the government, the private sector including the non-resident Keralite community, the local bodies, cooperatives and banks. It will shortlist transaction advisers and review progress quarterly as district-level meetings wrap up by December 12.

In line with the idea of creating a ‘partnership economy’ in a scenario where the State government’s resource-raising abilities are limited, the Kerala State Planning Board will soon have a Partnership Cell to explore investment opportunities by roping in multiple entities including the private sector and cooperatives.

Speaking to The Hindu in connection with Keralam’s upcoming 15th five-year Plan (2027-2032), Planning Board Vice-Chairman K.M. Chandrasekhar said the proposed cell will focus on forging partnerships among the government, the private sector including the non-resident Keralite community, the local bodies, cooperatives and banks.

The concept is founded on the idea that while the State government’s potential to raise financial resources is limited, Keralam as a State has wealth. The Board will short-list transaction advisers whose services can be used for various projects, Mr. Chandrasekhar, who is a former Union Cabinet Secretary, said.

Over the past few weeks, Planning Board officials have been conducting meetings in the districts as part of drawing up the 15th Plan. Meetings have been completed in ten districts and the Board hopes to cover the remaining four by December 12. The heads of the Planning Board’s divisions will be placed in charge of two districts each as part of the Partnership Cell’s activities. Once in three months there will be a plan review.

“The State does not have enough money to carry forward a meaningful development programme. We have already said in the White Paper (’Kerala’s Fiscal Health: A Status Report’ prepared by a team led by Mr. Chandrasekhar earlier this year) that 77% of our revenues go into salaries, interest and pensions. What remains again gets distributed on a number of welfare schemes. The actual expenditure of the State on capital is only about 1.34%. So, how do you generate investment? It’s a very simple economic formula that the more investment you put in the greater will be your return,” he said.

In mid-November, the Board had announced that the 15th Plan would aim to raise Keralam’s gross state domestic product (GSDP) from ₹16 lakh crore to ₹28 lakh crore, achieving a growth rate of 7% per year as opposed to the current 5%. Also, the Plan would be prepared in smart mode, where outcomes are ‘specific, measurable, achievable, result-oriented and time-bound.’

The Planning Board Vice-Chairman pointed to the recently-passed Simplified and Accelerated Regulatory Approvals and Licensing (SARAL) Keralam Bill, 2026, as a major step towards removing needless roadblocks in the path of potential investors.

articles.title: West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” alleged Bongaon MP Santanu Thakur

Amid reports of growing feuds within the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in West Bengal , Union Minister of State and Bongaon MP Shantanu Thakur not only publicly acknowledged factionalism within the party but also said that BJP supporters are attacked by its members.
The Minister spoke about developments in his own constituency in North 24 Parganas, but reports of factional feuds within the BJP rank and file have surfaced across the State.

“Here, BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” Mr. Thakur, who is the Bongaon MP and also a prominent leader of the Matua community, alleged.

The Minister, who hails from Thakurbari and is the religious head of the Matua community, said that divisions are emerging within the party, resulting in major problems. Differences between Shantanu Thakur, the Bongaon North MLA, and State Food and Civil Supplies Minister Ashok Kirtania have been going around in political circles.

On Sunday, BJP’s Panihati MLA Ratna Debnath, while expressing condolences over the death of a BJP worker, said that it would have been better “had the BJP not come to power in the State.” Arup Saha, husband of Ruma Saha—the secretary of BJP’s Panihati-1 Mandal (zone)—was attacked on Saturday (November 14, 2026), by a mob that allegedly included some of the party’s supporters. Saha succumbed to his injuries on Sunday.

Reports of an intra-party feud have surfaced between long-time supporters of the ruling party in the State and former Trinamool Congress supporters who switched allegiance after the Assembly election results in May 2026. Political observers say that the majority of the BJP leadership, including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, had joined the party about five to six years ago.

State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has repeatedly said that the doors of the party are closed for Trinamool supporters who want to join. Mr. Bhattacharya said that an FIR should be registered against elements who are trying to associate with the party and tarnish its image. “Register FIRs. Suvendu Adhikari is the police minister. Give me the papers; I will file them,” Mr. Bhattacharya said.

articles.title: What to know about the online banking delays affecting major U.S. banks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused problems throughout the financial system on Monday (November 16, 2026), resulting in thousands of customers reporting difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service Zelle.

JPMorgan Chase, the largest U.S. bank by total assets, said a software bug was affecting its internal hardware systems and causing transaction delays. The company was working to bring banking services back online.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, "Some services aren't available. We're working on them. Please try back later."

In a sense, yes. Customers at Bank of America, Citigroup and other banks trying to transact with Chase may have seen their transactions slow, even though those banks were not having issues with their services.
"Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," explained Joe Evangelisti, a spokesperson for Chase.
Zelle was not directly affected by the Chase glitch. But customers at other banks may have experienced transaction delays while trying to send or receive Zelle payments involving a Chase customer.

Zelle is a rapid peer-to-peer payment system used by major US banks. The platform is owned by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which in turn is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, US Bank and Wells Fargo.
A spokesperson for Early Warning Services said the Zelle network was fully operational.
Chase said that the technical problem was not the result of a cyberattack, stressing that it was an isolated incident and not related to anything other than a bug.
Chase said its customers still have access to their accounts and funds. The company expects the issue to be resolved by the end of day Monday.

articles.title: Singapore seeks ‘trusted access’ to AI chips after new US curbs
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Singapore is finding itself at the centre of the controversy as cloud computing firm Megaspeed, suspected of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls, is based there

Singapore said Tuesday (November 17, 2026) it was seeking “trusted access” to advanced AI chips after the United States imposed new curbs aimed at stopping Chinese firms from accessing the technology through overseas data centres.

The curbs came days after a spy scandal forced Jensen Huang to quit as Nvidia chief, as questions emerged over whether Singapore-based Megaspeed aided Chinese firms in accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips in violation of US rules.
“We are studying the details of this new measure carefully,” Singapore’s ministries overseeing digital development and energy, trade and industry said in a joint statement.
“We are engaging affected companies to understand the potential impact on their businesses,” the ministries added.

The city-state was also talking to the “relevant US authorities on the scope and implementation of the measure, as well as exploring how to facilitate trusted access for Singapore companies”, the ministries added.
One loophole allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

Under the new rule, data centres anywhere in the world will need a US licence to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.
The rule also requires licences to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which the US commerce department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.
Singapore is finding itself at the centre of the controversy as cloud computing firm Megaspeed, suspected of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls, is based there.

The scandal erupted on November 8 when The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang and Megaspeed executive Alice Huang -- who are not related -- were romantically linked, and that some within the US government suspected she might be a spy for China.

articles.title: Six arrested for running illegal LPG refilling unit in Hyderabad, 46 domestic cylinders seized
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hyderabad City Police arrested six persons for running an illegal LPG refilling unit at a scrap shop in Bapu Ghat, Langer Houz, and seized 46 domestic LPG cylinders, 36 small cylinders and refilling equipment worth approximately ₹4 lakh.

The Commissioner’s Task Force, Golconda Zone team, in a joint operation with Langer Houz police and the Assistant Civil Supplies Officer (ACSO), Mehdipatnam circle, raided the premises following credible information about the illegal activity.

According to the police, the accused were transferring LPG from domestic cylinders into smaller commercial cylinders of 3 kg and 5 kg capacity using refilling equipment, without taking necessary safety precautions. They were selling the refilled cylinders in the black market to customers to make illegal profits.

The police identified the arrested persons as Ravi (29), a resident of Langer Houz, Sohail (19) and Pankaj (20), both residents of Prashanth Nagar, Langer Houz, Vicky, a labourer and LPG cylinder supplier associated with an HP Gas agency, Ramu (32), an auto owner involved in supplying HP Gas cylinders from SK Agencies, Langer Houz and Raju (47), a labourer from Mangar Basti, Mallepally.

During the raid, the police seized 46 full domestic HP Gas cylinders, 35 empty 3 kg cylinders, one empty 5 kg cylinder, a weighing machine, seven gas-refilling kits and two trolley autos bearing registration numbers TG 13 T 1244 and TS 13 QA 9722. The total value of the seized property was estimated at ₹4 lakh.

articles.title: CJP leaders appear before SEM in Jantar Mantar tresspass case; Saurav Das’ Delhi address verified
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Second appearance since their release from Tihar jail on October 21; Das says Delhi Police took a month to verify his address, while Ranka hopes the club concept spreads across the country.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared before Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Ritu Raj at Delhi’s Mandir Marg police station on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) in connection with the Jantar Mantar trespassing case, with Mr. Das submitting documents to verify his residential address in the Capital.

The duo spent over three hours at the police station. Speaking to the media after the proceedings, Mr. Das said they had waited for about two hours for the Magistrate to arrive, after which the proceedings began.

“This hearing was basically for them to verify where in Delhi I live. It is a matter of fact that the Delhi Police is aware where I live, but for the last one month they haven’t been able to verify that. And they have a force of one lakh police officers. It’s surprising that one lakh officers are not able to verify where I live,” he said.
Mr. Das said he had now submitted the required documents and that his address had been verified. He added that the documents were submitted on the condition that they would not be leaked.
“The presiding Judge has given the order to ensure the documents don’t leak from either the court or the police’s side,” he said.
He also appealed to the media not to forward any documents pertaining to him if they received them, and instead share them with him so that the matter could be taken up in court.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das hit back at funding charges during CJP press meet

This was the duo’s second appearance before the SEM since their release from Tihar jail on October 21, following seven days in judicial custody. They had last appeared before the Magistrate on October 23, when Mr. Das was asked to furnish a verifiable document corroborating his present residential address in Delhi.

At the time of their release, the two had furnished personal and surety bonds and submitted written undertakings before the SEM that they would not call for any protest at Jantar Mantar as long as it remained a denotified protest site. They had also assured the court that they would not engage in any activity that could breach peace.
They were directed to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.

articles.title: SIR row: Supreme Court agrees to hear INDIA bloc’s ‘interrogatories’ on ‘nationwide SIR’, CEC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) agreed to have a detailed hearing of an application filed by Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders, who have posed 48 ‘interrogatories’ directly to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and senior poll officials regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The interrogatories challenge the veracity of “bare assertions” made by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in an institutional affidavit filed on October 26 . One of these assertions was that the decision to hold a nationwide SIR, which saw around 13 crore voters excluded from the electoral rolls, was “unanimous”.

The interrogatories intend to compel the two Election Commissioners to individually state on oath whether they had objected to the SIR orders. The interrogatories require the CEC, the Election Commissioners, and poll officials to support their every answer with documentary proof in court.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the case for December 9 after senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for the ECI, enquired if the court would have enough time to hear the multiple petitions in the post-lunch session.

Senior advocates Kapil Sibal, A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., for the INDIA bloc leaders, urged the Bench, which was about to rise for lunch after the morning session when Mr. Salve intervened, to issue notice on the application containing the interrogatories.

Though, initially, the court agreed to issue notice to the ECI for a response, Mr. Salve, along with senior advocate Maninder Singh, opposed the issuance of any notice before a preliminary hearing on the application.
“We will then hear the application and pass necessary orders,” the CJI said.

The application was filed as part of the Opposition leaders’ writ petition claiming the nationwide SIR exercise, the manner and extent of its conduct, was the product of a unilateral exercise of power by the CEC without the knowledge, approval or concurrence of the Election Commissioners.

Mr. Gandhi and the Opposition leaders submitted that posing the interrogatories was necessary as the controversy in their petition substantially rested upon facts that lie exclusively within the knowledge and the records of the ECI. The petitioners said they had no means of access to those facts except through the ECI and their officials.
So far, rather than disclosing those facts, the ECI has only made bare assertions.

The interrogatories challenge the veracity of “bare assertions” made by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in an institutional affidavit filed on October 26 . One of these assertions was that the decision to hold a nationwide SIR, which saw around 13 crore voters excluded from the electoral rolls, was “unanimous”.

The interrogatories intend to compel the two Election Commissioners to individually state on oath whether they had objected to the SIR orders. The interrogatories require the CEC, the Election Commissioners, and poll officials to support their every answer with documentary proof in court.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the case for December 9 after senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for the ECI, enquired if the court would have enough time to hear the multiple petitions in the post-lunch session.

fullParagraphs: The Nilgiris district administration has announced that the 5th Nilgiris Book Festival-2026 will be held from November 27 to December 6.

In a press release, the district administration said the book festival was part of the initiatives being undertaken by the State government to promote the habit of reading among school students and the general public. The festival is to be organised jointly by the Nilgiris district administration, the Public Libraries Department and the Booksellers and Publishers Association of South India (BAPASI) and will be held at the Resource Centre for Tribal Development on Garden Road in Udhagamandalam.

The book festival will take place over a period of 10 days and will be open to visitors from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. “More than 50 publishers, who are members of BAPASI, will participate in the festival and display their books for sale. Renowned speakers from across Tamil Nadu, along with writers from the Nilgiris district, will also participate in the event,” a press release added.

Various programmes, including book-related events, will be organised as part of the festival. These will include activities aimed at showcasing the talents of school and college students from the district, as well as cultural programmes, art performances and other literary activities, it was stated.
District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru requested members of the public, school and college students, and teachers to attend the festival.

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 17 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: Quad announces Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Quad is a ‘trusted partnership’ delivering solutions, says PM Modi

The Quad grouping, following its meeting in Manila, announced the ‘Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration’ which is “ a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness”
“In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added.
In a joint press release following the Quad meeting in Manila, the group said that it “affirms the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.”
“The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” it added.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed ways to strengthen cooperation and exchanged views on regional and global developments with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand in separate bilateral meetings in the Philippines.

Mr. Modi, who arrived in Manila on Monday to attend the ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit, met Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on the sidelines of the two summits.
PM Modi, at the Quad meeting in Manila, announced that the inaugural Quad Business Leaders Forum will be hosted in Mumbai in 2027, the Ministry of External Affairs said.

The Ministry of External Affairs said that at the Quad meeting, PM Modi “reaffirmed India’s commitment to a constructive and reliable Quad partnership, advancing peace, prosperity and resilience in the Indo-Pacific through cooperation in maritime security, economic security, critical technologies and disaster response.”

U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed four key outcomes of the Quad leaders’ meeting in Manila, covering economic cooperation, artificial intelligence, maritime security and cybersecurity, as leaders of India, the United States, Japan and Australia gathered for the high-level engagement.
The four outcomes include the Quad Business Leaders’ Forum, Super Intelligence Accelerator, Maritime Intelligence Sharing Corporation and Quad cybersecurity intelligence-sharing cooperation.

articles.title: Jensen Huang | AI rainmaker meets his Waterloo
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Nvidia chief’s abrupt exit marks a stunning fall from grace for the man who built the hardware foundation of the AI revolution, forged deep ties with Silicon Valley’s tech leaders and expanded the company’s reach across every layer of the AI stack

“In another life, Jensen Huang might have been a teacher,” says Tae Kim in his book The Nvidia Way . Whether he likes it or not, the Nvidia co-founder’s reality has now been reset, forcing him back to his idiosyncratic style of solving problems: diagramming on a whiteboard. But this time he won’t get a clean start as the scandal-hit former chief of Nvidia will face intense scrutiny over his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who is at the centre of an alleged spy scandal.

Within days of reports emerging about Mr. Huang’s affair with Alice Huang , The New York Times reported a second relationship, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s head of healthcare and one of his direct reports. By then, the controversy had come to a head, forcing Mr. Huang to resign as CEO of Nvidia, the company he had built from scratch.

articles.title: Fresh unrest in Bangladesh as garment workers protest, block highways for higher wages
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways

Authorities in Bangladesh on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) deployed more than 1,000 paramilitary personnel as garment workers staged demonstrations and clashed with police in the industrial belt around Dhaka, demanding higher wages and blocking three major highways.

Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways, disrupting traffic and causing long tailbacks.
The demonstrations are part of weeks of intermittent protests that began in late October across Bangladesh's major garment-producing areas.
The workers have been demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage from the existing Tk 12,500 ($100) to Tk 30,000 ($240), citing rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare.

Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for more than 80% of the country's export earnings, with prolonged disruption threatening production schedules, international buyers' confidence and global apparel supply chains.
In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) said it had deployed 42 platoons of personnel in the industrial hubs of Ashulia, Gazipur and Narayanganj. Officials said the personnel were also using drones to maintain surveillance over readymade garment factory workers.

Police said two of the three highways had been cleared, but intermittent blockades continued to cause heavy traffic congestion on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway. "We are working to clear the highways and disperse the protesters," a police spokesperson said.

The industrial unrest also affected factory operations. Police said at least 37 garment factories across the industrial belt were declared closed on Tuesday, while dozens more temporarily suspended production after workers left their workplaces to join demonstrations.

In Dhaka, garment workers gathered in the Darus Salam and Shah Ali police station areas of Mirpur on Tuesday morning and attempted to move towards the Mirpur-10 roundabout, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.

articles.title: Burnham delays tabling of options for U.K.-EU ties
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: At Friday’s Summit Mr. Burnham said he seek to finalise an agreement with Brussels for closer U.K.-EU ties, based on the groundwork laid by his predecessor Keir Starmer

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has delayed unveiling options for long-term ties between the U.K.- and EU The Prime Minister had said in September that he would set out options — including the option of a complete return to the EU — around the U.K.-EU Summit, which is scheduled for Friday.

“This will take time and we will present those options and our assessment of them to inform decisions in the next Parliament,” Mr. Burnham said on Monday at the annual City Hall banquet in the capital’s financial hub.
“At every stage, the British people will be the boss,” he added.

At Friday’s Summit Mr. Burnham said he seek to finalise an agreement with Brussels for closer U.K.-EU ties, based on the groundwork laid by his predecessor Keir Starmer. Mr. Burnham suggested this deal could increase the U.K.’s GDP by 0.4%.

Legislation for the deal will be presented to the U.K. Parliament next week, the Prime Minister said, as he ruled out crossing red lines, i.e., ruling out joining the EU, allowing the “free movement” of EU citizens across the border or taking the U.K. into the EU Customs Union and Single Market during this Parliament (which ends in 2029).

EU Affairs Minister Hamish Falconer said that a U.K.-EU agreement would involve an “exit clause” in case a future U.K. government run by the Conservatives or Reform U.K. undid the deal, the BBC reported. These two opposition parties have said they would undo any agreement reached by Labour. The exit clause it is likely to involve payments to Brussels to set up border infrastructure.
During his speech Mr. Burnham also spoke of reviving the Commonwealth (of which India is also a part) group of nations.
“It is a unique geopolitical forum, not including either the US or China, and yet we have failed to invest energy in modernising the Commonwealth,” he said.
The Prime Minister said Britain would offer countries a structured dialogue in 2027 on its historical role in slavery but would not make financial reparations for it.

“It is basic good manners, if a friend wants to talk about something that is unjust and unresolved, to listen and engage,” he said. Longstanding calls from Caribbean nations for reparations and apologies grew louder in recent weeks, around a visit of King Charles III to the region.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has delayed unveiling options for long-term ties between the U.K.- and EU The Prime Minister had said in September that he would set out options — including the option of a complete return to the EU — around the U.K.-EU Summit, which is scheduled for Friday.

“This will take time and we will present those options and our assessment of them to inform decisions in the next Parliament,” Mr. Burnham said on Monday at the annual City Hall banquet in the capital’s financial hub.

“At every stage, the British people will be the boss,” he added.

At Friday’s Summit Mr. Burnham said he seek to finalise an agreement with Brussels for closer U.K.-EU ties, based on the groundwork laid by his predecessor Keir Starmer. Mr. Burnham suggested this deal could increase the U.K.’s GDP by 0.4%.

Legislation for the deal will be presented to the U.K. Parliament next week, the Prime Minister said, as he ruled out crossing red lines, i.e., ruling out joining the EU, allowing the “free movement” of EU citizens across the border or taking the U.K. into the EU Customs Union and Single Market during this Parliament (which ends in 2029).

EU Affairs Minister Hamish Falconer said that a U.K.-EU agreement would involve an “exit clause” in case a future U.K. government run by the Conservatives or Reform U.K. undid the deal, the BBC reported. These two opposition parties have said they would undo any agreement reached by Labour. The exit clause it is likely to involve payments to Brussels to set up border infrastructure.

“It is a unique geopolitical forum, not including either the US or China, and yet we have failed to invest energy in modernising the Commonwealth,” he said.

articles.title: Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent, eight people arrested
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The incident occurred when Forest personnel tried to guide a female elephant, separated from a herd, back to the jungle it came from

Eight people were detained in central Assam’s Hojai district after they clashed with Forest Department personnel on Monday night (November 16, 2026) during an operation to guide a female elephant back to the jungle it came from.

The Forest officials fired “sera bullets” (pellets) from a pump-action gun to divert the elephant away from a human settlement. Five people were injured in the firing, triggering the mob violence and leaving two personnel injured.
Forest officials claimed three people sustained pellet injuries. The injured, including one of the two personnel, were admitted to a local hospital for treatment.

Divisional Forest Officer Nayan Jyoti Rajbongshi said a herd of elephants from the hills of Karbi Anglong entered the Hawaipur Reserve Forest in Hojai on Monday morning. Barring the female elephant, estimated to be 40 years old, the herd returned to Karbi Anglong a few hours later.
“We received information about the movement of the female elephant, possibly separated from the herd, along a road in a revenue area. We managed to push it into the Hawaipur Reserve Forest,” he said.
However, the elephant emerged from the forest around dusk and headed toward a village. The Forest personnel fired the pellets to drive it away, but some villagers were injured in the process.
“The police brought the situation under control and picked up eight people who clashed with our personnel. The police recorded the statement of our personnel,” Mr. Rajbongshi said.
Wildlife officials said people often obstruct rescue operations by gathering around a wild animal that strays out of a forest.
According to Assam government data tabled in the 126-member Assembly in July, as many as 1,147 people and 246 elephants were killed in human-elephant conflicts in the State since 2016.

articles.title: Rights beyond the pad: making menstrual health services work in every school

fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has recognised menstrual health as a constitutional right and laid down obligations for schools and governments. The real challenge now is making these services function reliably, every month, in every school

The Supreme Court’s January 2026 judgment in Dr. Jaya Thakur v. Government of India recognised menstrual health as part of the right to life under Article 21 and directed States and Union Territories to provide free sanitary napkins, functional gender-segregated toilets, usable water and safe menstrual waste disposal facilities in every government and private school.

The success of this judgment, however, will not be measured in courtrooms. It will be measured in whether a girl can access a sanitary napkin, use a clean toilet with running water and dispose of menstrual waste safely.

articles.title: Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.

The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected three Indian space companies to develop High-Resolution Indian Human Settlement Layers (IHSL) across Indian cities.

The three companies, SpacePixxel Technologies Pvt. Ltd. , KaleidEO Space Systems Pvt. Ltd. and Azista Industries Pvt. Ltd. have been selected under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme for Use Case Demonstration by Non-Government Entities (NGEi) to develop IHSL across Indian cities.

These companies will collectively receive seed funding of ₹1.46 crore to develop and demonstrate an indigenous satellite-based system for 3D reconstruction of India’s built environment using monocular imageries.

IN-SPACe said that the initiative, undertaken under the Announcement of Opportunity (AO) for the development of high-resolution IHSL, aims to address the NITI Aayog’s requirement of having an accurate and detailed geospatial data on human settlement which can be used for urban planning, infrastructure development and disaster risk assessment in addition to population assessment.

The selected companies will develop models using Earth Observation data to generate three integrated outputs covering built-up surface and building type, building height, and built-up volume. The deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.
The techniques will be developed at a high spatial resolution using Indian satellite data.

The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, representing distinct urban contexts of a large metropolitan region and a hill city. The pilot project will derive settlement patterns across two time periods, enabling comparisons of urban growth and changes in built-up density over time.

“India’s cities are expanding rapidly, both horizontally and vertically. Effective urban planning requires an accurate understanding of the built environment, but critical data gaps often limit this. This initiative addresses that gap by bringing together Indian satellite data, indigenous technology and clearly defined requirements from government departments. It gives Indian companies an opportunity to develop solutions for real-world urban challenges. More importantly, successful pilots can lay the foundation for scalable, homegrown capabilities that can be deployed across Indian cities,” Dr. Pawan Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe, said.

“Starting with Bengaluru and Shimla, this IN-SPACe supported project will provide pathways to build indigenous satellite data on human settlements, allowing recognition of urbanisation as it happens.” said Shamika Ravi, Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)
Rajeev Jyoti, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, said that the technical evaluation process was highly competitive, with 26 proposals received.

articles.title: Nvidia to reveal first earnings since spy scandal
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis
AI chip giant Nvidia reports its first earnings on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) since a spy scandal forced co-founder Jensen Huang to quit and the United States to tighten export curbs on chips.
Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

Mr. Huang, perhaps the tech industry's most recognised booster of AI, stepped down on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The scandal has battered shares of Nvidia -- until recently the world's most valuable publicly traded company -- which is at the centre of an AI buildout that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe.

Washington announced new restrictions on Monday (November 16) on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing just before the high-profile APEC summit where U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are set for talks.
Beijing's Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: "China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests".

The new U.S. export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi's talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, which starts Wednesday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington's new rules, data centres anywhere in the world will need a U.S. license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under U.S. arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil -- countries the U.S. commerce department says present a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on U.S. hardware not available for export to China.

Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis

AI chip giant Nvidia reports its first earnings on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) since a spy scandal forced co-founder Jensen Huang to quit and the United States to tighten export curbs on chips.

Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

Mr. Huang, perhaps the tech industry's most recognised booster of AI, stepped down on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The scandal has battered shares of Nvidia -- until recently the world's most valuable publicly traded company -- which is at the centre of an AI buildout that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe.

Washington announced new restrictions on Monday (November 16) on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing just before the high-profile APEC summit where U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are set for talks.

Beijing's Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: "China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests".

The new U.S. export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi's talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, which starts Wednesday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington's new rules, data centres anywhere in the world will need a U.S. license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under U.S. arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil -- countries the U.S. commerce department says present a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on U.S. hardware not available for export to China.

articles.title: In line with WHO framework, T.N.’s National Centre of Ageing provides integrated care for the elderly
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: WHO’s approach is to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care

Maintaining physical and mental capacities is key to ensuring that older persons remain functionally independent. With age-related conditions such as visual and hearing impairment, memory and mobility issues often remaining undetected or unaddressed in the elderly, the National Centre of Ageing (NCA), Guindy has started to focus on providing integrated care to help older persons maintain functional ability. This is in line with the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) integrated care for older people approach (ICOPE).

According to the WHO, numerous physiological changes occur, and the risks of experiencing a decline in physical and mental capacities (intrinsic capacity) and having more than one condition (disease) increase when people age. This could manifest as cognitive decline, limited mobility, hearing loss, malnutrition, vision impairment, depressive symptoms, urinary incontinence and falls. ICOPE is WHO’s approach to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care. It supports optimising intrinsic capacity and functional ability in older age, it said.

articles.title: Keralam to inform HC on tourist bus colour change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision was taken at a meeting of the STA held on Tuesday, following an interim order of the High Court and after taking into account the views of bus owners and other stakeholders

The State government will inform the High Court on November 19 of its decision to modify the uniform white colour scheme mandated for tourist buses in Keralam. The decision was taken at a meeting of the State Transport Authority (STA) held here on Tuesday, following an interim order of the High Court and after taking into account the views of bus owners and other stakeholders.

The uniform white colour scheme for tourist buses was strictly enforced in the State following the Vadakkencherry bus accident in Palakkad in 2022. However, bus owners have complained that the regulation has pushed the State’s tourist bus sector into a severe crisis, as buses from other States operating under All India Permits are not subject to similar restrictions.

This has put vehicles registered in Keralam at a competitive disadvantage, affecting their business and the livelihoods of thousands of workers. In view of these concerns and representations from bus owners, the government issued a notification last September proposing a reconsideration of the colour scheme requirement.

Meanwhile, any relaxation in the colour regulations will not affect the enforcement of safety standards. Tourist buses will not be allowed to display oversized images, graphics or advertisements on their exteriors if these could cause inconvenience to other road users. Fitness certificates will not be issued to vehicles fitted with unauthorised LED lights, strip lights or halogen lamps. The display of advertisements to promote services will also be prohibited.

The meeting decided to ensure strict compliance with safety standards in accordance with a 2019 High Court order and the Central Motor Vehicles Act. The meeting was attended by Transport Commissioner G. Sparjan Kumar, IG P. Prakash and government nominee K. Suresh Babu.

articles.title: Minister calls for unity among alliance leaders to ensure victory in panchayat polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing NDA partners from Owk and Banaganapalle mandals, Janardhan Reddy expresses hope that the alliance government will continue its winning streak at the village level as well with the blessings of the public

Roads and Buildings (R&B) Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy has expressed confidence that the candidates supported by the NDA will certainly achieve a resounding victory in the upcoming panchayat elections.

Continuing his discussions with the leaders of NDA partners ahead of the sarpanch elections, Mr. Janardhan Reddy on Tuesday held meeting with the leaders from Owk and Banaganapalle mandals. During the discussions, he highlighted that the public had faith in the alliance government, and with their blessings, would continue their winning streak at the village level as well.

During the meeting, discussions were also held regarding the political landscape in each village of the mandal, election preparedness, the selection of candidates, and coordination among the alliance parties.

The Minister noted that the alliance government, under the leadership of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, was focussing on development as well as public welfare. He said the government was upholding the public’s trust by fulfilling the promises made during the elections. He added that the positive sentiment among the public on the government’s performance would be reflected in the panchayat elections.

He urged the leaders of the alliance parties at the village level to work in coordination, setting aside personal differences. The Minister called for a collective effort to strengthen the NDA in every village of the two mandals and to ensure its victory in the upcoming panchayat polls.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan moves slowly, likely to intensify further by November 18 morning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Probable landfall between Visakhapatnam and Nellore; isolated heavy rain likely in Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam and Vizianagaram from November 18 evening
Cyclonic storm Akvan (meaning ‘demon’ in Persian) over the central parts of the south and west-central Bay of Bengal may intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday morning.

Initially, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast that the weather system would strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening, but the system had either remained stationary or moved slowly.

At 5.30 p.m., the weather system was centred around 590 km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 650 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 650 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 780 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.

It may continue to move slowly north-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal on Wednesday morning, and further into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning.

The system has changed its track slightly, and the probable landfall points may remain between Visakhapatnam and Nellore. Isolated heavy rainfall is likely in the northern districts of Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, and strong winds with speeds of 100 kmph to 110 kmph are likely along the coastal belt from Wednesday evening.

Andhra Pradesh is experiencing a very rare event, since it is not often that a State sees three tropical cyclones crossing its coast within a month, said IMD Director General of Meteorology Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.

Speaking to The Hindu over the phone, he said it is normal for the Bay of Bengal to see three or four tropical cyclones in a year. “What is not normal is that all of them are crossing the coast near Andhra Pradesh.”

A similar event last happened in 1987. And, the reason for this can be attributed to El Nino, he said. “Both 1987 and 2026 have strong similarities. 1987 was a strong El Nino year, with drought conditions. And 2026 is one too,” he said.
Mr. Mohapatra explained that El Nino influences the formation of cyclones in such a way that more of these develop over the southern latitude, which may move towards A.P.
Handling a disaster of this kind has become challenging for the State.

articles.title: Assam’s Karbi Anglong sets Guinness record with 15,000 dancers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is the second world record for folk music and dance forms in the Northeast within a week

About 15,000 dancers representing different communities of Assam’s Karbi Anglong district set a Guinness World Record on Monday evening (November 17, 2026), the second such feat for folk music and dance in the northeastern region within a week.
Garo community drummers in Meghalaya set a world record on November 14 by playing 1,000 damas (elongated drums) during the Wangala Festival in Tura, the State’s second-largest urban centre.

“History created. Karbi Anglong has made its mark on the world stage!” Tuliram Ronghang, the Chief Executive Member of the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council (KAAC) said in a social media post after an official adjudicator of Guinness World Records announced the achievement.
The record was set at the Karbi Anglong Sports Association Stadium in Diphu, about 250 km east of Guwahati, during the district’s 75th anniversary celebrations organised by the KAAC.
Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma congratulated the participants ahead of joining the third and final day of the celebrations on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

This is the second world record for folk music and dance forms in the Northeast within a week

About 15,000 dancers representing different communities of Assam’s Karbi Anglong district set a Guinness World Record on Monday evening (November 17, 2026), the second such feat for folk music and dance in the northeastern region within a week.

Garo community drummers in Meghalaya set a world record on November 14 by playing 1,000 damas (elongated drums) during the Wangala Festival in Tura, the State’s second-largest urban centre.

“History created. Karbi Anglong has made its mark on the world stage!” Tuliram Ronghang, the Chief Executive Member of the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council (KAAC) said in a social media post after an official adjudicator of Guinness World Records announced the achievement.

The record was set at the Karbi Anglong Sports Association Stadium in Diphu, about 250 km east of Guwahati, during the district’s 75th anniversary celebrations organised by the KAAC.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma congratulated the participants ahead of joining the third and final day of the celebrations on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

articles.title: Some Congress leaders stalled probe into Modi in Gujarat riots case, claims Veerappa Moily
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Former Chief Minister and former Union Minister M. Veerappa Moily on Tuesday alleged that some Congress leaders in the then UPA government had stalled the investigation into Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the alleged 2002 Gujarat riots case when he was the Chief Minister of the State.

Speaking after releasing Sonia Gandhi’s book Belonging – A Journey of Love at the KPCC office in Bengaluru, Mr. Moily said, “Home Minister Amit Shah was the first one to go to jail. He would not have become the Home Minister and the powerful leader he is now. His case was tried outside Gujarat, and he was living in exile.”

Mr. Shah was arrested by the CBI in 2010 in connection with the alleged Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case. In December 2014, a special court in Mumbai discharged him, citing lack of evidence. Mr. Moily was the Union Law Minister during 2010-11.

“Next would have been Mr. Modi. He would have been exiled, but our own [UPA] government stalled the inquiry... the investigation. Not [the then Prime Minister] Manmohan Singh, but some other leaders. Now we are experiencing it under Mr. Modi. But I don’t want to give details now,” Mr. Moily said.

Following a Supreme Court directive in 2009, a Special Investigation Team (SIT) questioned Mr. Modi in 2010 regarding an alleged larger conspiracy during the 2002 riots. In 2012, the SIT gave a clean chit to Mr. Modi.

He said Ms. Gandhi, as UPA chairperson, had constituted a committee under his chairmanship to study the future challenges facing the Congress. Rahul Gandhi, Digvijaya Singh and Ghulam Nabi Azad were among its members. When the first report was submitted, Ms. Gandhi told him that “some party leaders are opposing it”, he said.

“There were leaders in our party who wanted to maintain the status quo and did not want change. Mr. Modi would not have come to power if the reforms had been implemented as desired by Ms. Gandhi,” Mr. Moily said.

He also took a dig at Congress leaders from Tamil Nadu, saying they had opposed joining the M. Karunanidhi-led government even though the party had won a good number of Assembly seats. “Some leaders from Tamil Nadu wanted positions in Delhi and not in Tamil Nadu,” he said.
Mr. Moily said no one used to take Ms. Gandhi seriously before she became AICC president.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah were not present at the book launch event.

articles.title: Karnataka has a ‘goonda government’, says Ashok
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Alleging a rise in “goondaism” in the State after D.K. Shivakumar became Chief Minister, Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R. Ashok on Tuesday claimed that BJP workers active on social media were being targeted by the police through the registration of false cases.

Speaking to reporters in H.D. Kote, Mr. Ashok said BJP activists on social media in different parts of the State, including Bidar, Kalaburagi and Bagalkot, were being summoned by the police and forced to furnish bonds of ₹5 lakh for expressing their views.

Though the right to freedom of speech and expression is a constitutional right in a democracy, the police were booking cases only against BJP workers while sparing Congress workers, who also expressed themselves, he alleged.

There was no such political vendetta when the BJP was in power, he said, and warned the police that the party, when it returned to power, would take action against them if they did not stop their alleged atrocities against BJP workers. After Mr. Shivakumar assumed office as Chief Minister, the State appeared to be under an “indirect Emergency”, he said, adding that it looked like Karnataka had a “goonda government”.

Criticising Mr. Shivakumar for “spending most of his time in Delhi”, Mr. Ashok said the Chief Minister had no concern for farmers in distress owing to drought and alleged that farmer suicides in the State had increased.

Earlier, the Leader of the Opposition participated in the Jayanti celebrations of revolutionary freedom fighter and tribal leader Bhagwan Birsa Munda, organised by the BJP ST Morcha at Ankanathapura Hadi in H.D. Kote.
He said Bhagwan Birsa Munda had raised his voice for tribal communities and fought for their rights.

articles.title: India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government

Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that India or any other country could not dictate terms over deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s return home.
Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government.
Talking to reporters at the Bangladesh Secretariat, Mr. Zahed said, “Bangladesh is now an independent, sovereign state standing on firm legal ground and it will reject any unjust terms.”
The premier’s Adviser, however, said he did not believe India would attach conditions to returning Hasina.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Hasina's extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.
He further said: “India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh."
Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal convicted Hasina in November 2025 of crimes against humanity for her role in the crackdown on protesters during the July-August 2024 uprising.
Tried in absentia, she was sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Hasina has rejected the charges and the proceedings.

In a report last week, BBC Bangla said unnamed Indian officials indicated that New Delhi set two main conditions to facilitate Hasina’s return amid Dhaka’s repeated insistence on her extradition under a bilateral treaty despite her repeated stated plan to return home voluntarily to face the legal procedure.
The report said that “under the conditions, India wanted Bangladesh Army to directly receive Hasina either via a military flight to Delhi or at a land border crossing”.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Quad is a ‘trusted partnership’ delivering solutions, says PM Modi

Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed for New Delhi after concluding his two-day visit to the Philippines, during which he attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit and a meeting of the Quad leaders.
Mr. Modi also met Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., and the two leaders discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment.
The Prime Minister also discussed regional and global issues of mutual interest with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand on the sidelines of the visit.

Leaders of ‌the four-nation Quad grouping ⁠strongly oppose any destabilising or ‌unilateral actions that seek ‌to ‌change ⁠the status ⁠quo, including by force or coercion, which ‌escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and ‌stability, a joint statement said.
The leaders also ‌expressed grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary ‌export restrictions, the statement added after their ⁠meeting in Manila.

The Quad grouping, following its meeting in Manila, announced the ‘Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration’ which is “ a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness”
“In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added.
In a joint press release following the Quad meeting in Manila, the group said that it “affirms the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.”
“The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” it added.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed ways to strengthen cooperation and exchanged views on regional and global developments with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand in separate bilateral meetings in the Philippines.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed for New Delhi after concluding his two-day visit to the Philippines, during which he attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit and a meeting of the Quad leaders.

Leaders of ‌the four-nation Quad grouping ⁠strongly oppose any destabilising or ‌unilateral actions that seek ‌to ‌change ⁠the status ⁠quo, including by force or coercion, which ‌escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and ‌stability, a joint statement said.

“In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time improves an already perfect classic
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: One of the best Zelda games, Ocarina of Time, has got a gorgeous new remake that is worth playing, if you have a Switch 2

Remakes of past games are pure genius. There are several titles that were mega hits in the 90s or early 2000s when both silicon and game engines were breaking new ground in 3D. Many of those games do not hold up today as well as the pixel game era of the NES and SNES eras do.

Capcom has shown the world that remaking most of their lineup of Resident Evils has been successful. Ubisoft did it too, with Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag Resynced . No one expected Nintendo to jump into the fray, but they did and with style, not only remaking a Zelda game, but one of the cult favorites from the Nintendo 64 era. A game so loved, that it is continuously ranked as one of the greatest games of all times, which is a risky move to remake.
Fortunately, the Ocarina of Time remake not only wears that crown proudly, but is also the only game this year to challenge the sales might of the neon clad tsunami that is Grand Theft Auto VI .

Another saga begins in the cyclic battle of good versus evil, and it revolves around the only boy in the village without a fairy. Entrusted with the fate of the world Link must stop the evil Ganondorf who is intent on grabbing the Tri-force — an artefact that grants the bearer immense power. Guided by the enigmatic fairy Navi, Link must leave the safety of his home, Kokiri Forest, and journey across the sprawling expanse of Hyrule Field, venturing through perilous dungeons, and shift between childhood and adulthood to claim the Master Sword and become the Hero of Time.

Jumping between time from Link’s adult self to his child form is so meta, it will make you feel like you too are jumping through time with him. As an adult, tethered by responsibilities of adulting, you get to jump back to your childhood — something that is more poignant than nostalgia.

In comparison to some of the more sweeping, complex narratives of today’s fantasy games, Ocarina of Time harks back to a simplistic form of storytelling, which was mostly due to cartridge size restrictions. However, it is a template that many of Zelda’s best games have been set on. First-time players are sure to find Link’s story a refreshing one that focuses on core gameplay mechanics and a beautiful reimagining of the world.

The world is gorgeous and while it is not quite open, it does feel like it has got a lot of freedom of movement. It is great to explore all the temples filled with its well-created puzzles that you may remember the solutions for and see the new renditions of iconic places such as Death Mountain, Hyrule Field, Temple of Time and other faithful to their original designs, but are now a lot more fleshed out.
Much of the world has a lot more detail. So rather than rushing through the game, take in your surroundings and scrutinise houses, because there is environmental storytelling peppered everywhere.

Much of the game has been faithfully translated, but thankfully it is free from the oddities of that N64 controller. In addition to updated control mechanics, there are a lot of quality of life improvements, and those who have played Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom , may find the controls familiar. The motions are fluid, and there are some physics-based systems at play, that make everything from the sword clashes feel solid to the sensation of things being physically there in the world as they bounce around.

Combat gains quality of life improvements, inheriting motion aiming from its predecessors making it more snappy, lively and reactive. It lets you acrobatically dodge, backflip and attack enemies, and hits do feel like they actually connect. The enemy AI and animations have been changed to make those fights all the more nail-biting. This being the Switch 2, there are also motion controls to help you use Hookshot, Longshots, bows for some more dynamic ranged combat, if you preferred using this in the newer Zelda games. The addition of jump mechanics do change the dungeons a bit, meaning instead of having the original jump in certain zones, now you actually have to platform across.

articles.title: Hospital in Chennai performs complex aortic surgery on 10-year-old boy with rare vascular disease
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The child recovered and was discharged on the ninth day after surgery

A 10-year-old with a rare inflammatory blood vessel disease underwent surgery at SIMS Hospital, Chennai, to repair a large aneurysm of the aortic arch, the hospital said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The patient was diagnosed with aortoarteritis, also known as Takayasu arteritis, a condition that causes inflammation and narrowing or enlargement of blood vessels. The aneurysm had enlarged significantly, causing breathing difficulty, palpitations, and difficulty lying down. The risk of rupture made urgent surgery necessary. The patient weighed about 18 kg, adding to the technical challenges of the operation. As the aneurysm was located close to the breastbone, opening the chest through the usual approach carried a risk of injuring the enlarged aorta. The surgical team first connected the patient to a heart-lung machine through blood vessels in the groin.

The patient’s body was cooled to 16°C using a technique known as deep hypothermic circulatory arrest. Blood circulation was then temporarily stopped for about 40 minutes, enabling surgeons to remove the affected section of the aorta and replace it with a Dacron graft. Lowering the body temperature reduces metabolic activity and the organs’ oxygen requirements, helping protect them during the period when blood flow is interrupted.

The patient was subsequently rewarmed, restoring his blood circulation. Post-operative assessments showed no damage to the brain, kidneys, intestines, or spinal cord, the hospital said. The patient has resumed normal activities without breathing difficulty but will require continued medication and monitoring to control the underlying inflammation and prevent further aneurysms.

The surgery was performed by a team led by Bashi V. Velayudhan, director and senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, along with Mohammed Idhrees, senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, and a team of anaesthesiologists and other specialists.

The child recovered and was discharged on the ninth day after surgery

A 10-year-old with a rare inflammatory blood vessel disease underwent surgery at SIMS Hospital, Chennai, to repair a large aneurysm of the aortic arch, the hospital said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The patient was diagnosed with aortoarteritis, also known as Takayasu arteritis, a condition that causes inflammation and narrowing or enlargement of blood vessels. The aneurysm had enlarged significantly, causing breathing difficulty, palpitations, and difficulty lying down. The risk of rupture made urgent surgery necessary. The patient weighed about 18 kg, adding to the technical challenges of the operation. As the aneurysm was located close to the breastbone, opening the chest through the usual approach carried a risk of injuring the enlarged aorta. The surgical team first connected the patient to a heart-lung machine through blood vessels in the groin.

The patient’s body was cooled to 16°C using a technique known as deep hypothermic circulatory arrest. Blood circulation was then temporarily stopped for about 40 minutes, enabling surgeons to remove the affected section of the aorta and replace it with a Dacron graft. Lowering the body temperature reduces metabolic activity and the organs’ oxygen requirements, helping protect them during the period when blood flow is interrupted.

The patient was subsequently rewarmed, restoring his blood circulation. Post-operative assessments showed no damage to the brain, kidneys, intestines, or spinal cord, the hospital said. The patient has resumed normal activities without breathing difficulty but will require continued medication and monitoring to control the underlying inflammation and prevent further aneurysms.

The surgery was performed by a team led by Bashi V. Velayudhan, director and senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, along with Mohammed Idhrees, senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, and a team of anaesthesiologists and other specialists.
